Il calcule le volume de la sphère, appro: He calculated the volume of the sphere, approximated π and gave his name to a screw that probably existed before him. According to Plutarch, he was killed by a Roman soldier because he refused to follow him before finishing his problem. “Do not disturb my circles” appears in no ancient text.
Il pointe une lunette vers le ciel en 16: He pointed a telescope at the sky in 1609 and saw the moons of Jupiter, the phases of Venus and the mountains of the Moon. Condemned in 1633, he ended his days under house arrest. The “Eppur si muove” is probably a legend.
Gravitation, optique, calcul infinitésim: Gravitation, optics, calculus. He also ran the Royal Mint, had counterfeiters hanged and lost a fortune in the South Sea Company bubble. According to a witness quoted by Joseph Spence, he said he could not “calculate the madness of people.”
Il nomme l'oxygène, prouve que l'eau est: He named oxygen, proved that water is a compound and established the conservation of mass, with the help of Marie-Anne Paulze, his wife and collaborator. A tax farmer, he was guillotined in 1794. “The Republic has no need of scientists” is an apocryphal phrase.
Seule personne à avoir reçu deux prix No: The only person to have received two Nobel Prizes in two different sciences, physics in 1903 and chemistry in 1911. Her notebooks are still radioactive: the Bibliothèque nationale only makes them available under a very strict protocol.
